stemBlocks.value: Two brands of rice are sold as Brand A: 5 kg for $1 750 and Brand B: 8 kg for $2 880. (a) Calculate the cost per kilogram for each brand. (b) Which brand is the better buy? (c) How much would a customer save when buying 16 kg of the cheaper brand instead of the more expensive one?
Think first: The packs are different sizes, so the only fair comparison is the cost of one kilogram.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p023-q27 from workbook page 23.

solutionSteps.instruction: Find Brand A's cost per kilogram.
Find Brand B's cost per kilogram.

strategyBlocks.value: Divide each pack price by its mass to get a cost per kilogram, choose the smaller, then cost 16 kg both ways and subtract.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) Brand A $350 per kg, Brand B $360 per kg  (b) Brand A is the better buy  (c) The customer saves $160

whyThisWorks.value: Unit cost strips away pack size so two different offers can be ranked on a single scale. Once the gap per kilogram is known, the saving on any quantity is that gap multiplied by the quantity, so $10 per kg over 16 kg gives $160 directly. Costing both baskets in full is the safer route under exam pressure.

commonErrors.misconception: Assuming the larger pack must be cheaper per kilogram.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Assuming the larger pack must be cheaper per kilogram.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing the mass by the price instead of the price by the mass.

commonErrors.misconception: Finding the saving on one kilogram and forgetting to scale it to 16 kg.

examTip.value: Write units beside every number, such as $ per kg rather than just 350. A wrong division then becomes obvious as you write it.
